title: Tenant fairness burn-rate policy and quantized-variant rollout checklist
creator: Priya Patel
description: PRD excerpt and scope: Define a tenant-fair error-budget burn-rate policy and a stepwise rollout checklist for serving quantized model variants. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout gates for progressive activation of int8/4-bit variants across hosted and dedicated deployments. It clarifies scope (hosted API + Dedicated; excludes Private on-prem air-gapped installs for this phase), surface-level telemetry requirements, and the minimal dashboard/alerting that must exist before canary starts. Also lists trade-offs between cost savings and potential tail-latency regressions and defines rollback expectations.
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions: p50/p95/p99 latency envelopes per workload class (interactive chat, embeddings, batch) published to the console; target p99 <= 800ms for chat on dedicated capacity under nominal load.
Availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted model endpoints and 99.9% for dedicated pools while quantized variant is in canary. Any drop below 99.8% triggers immediate canary pause.

Error budget policy: monthly error budget defined per tenant weight. A tenant-level burn-rate calculator must be available and tested; automated soft-throttles applied when tenant burn rate > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes.
Tenant fairness: rollout must include weighted traffic steering so that no single tenant exceeds 3x their historical token rate during canary sampling windows.

Canary gating: prometheus alerts must be in place for p99 latency increase > 20% absolute or error rate increase > 0.5% (absolute) compared to baseline; two consecutive 5-minute buckets trigger rollback flag.
Quality guards: end-to-end regen-eval on 1k seeded prompts showing no regression in BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity beyond defined thresholds (documented in Confluence) before broad rollout.
Observability: dashboards for per-tenant burn, p50/p95/p99, successful tokens/sec, and model variant distribution exist and are linked in the PRD.
Operational playbook: runbook page created with steps for pausing rollout, resharding traffic, and emergency revert with contact on-call rotation.
Canary duration and ramp: initial canary window 1 hour at 1% sample traffic (weighted across 5 tenants), progressive ramps to 10% over 48h if no alerts; must pass automated checks at each step.
Release checklist: GitHub PR for runtime kernels approved, quantized model artifact checksum verified, canary infra terraform reviewed and merged before activation.
notes: Scope clarification: Private (air-gapped) deployments will require a separate validation matrix; excluded to reduce compliance burden for initial rollout.
Trade-offs: Aggressive quantization gives 30-45% cost reduction on token compute but risks tail-latency regressions on long sequences. We prefer conservative initial ramps for chat workloads.
Data retention/telemetry: store per-tenant latency histograms for 30 days to enable post-mortem correlation with quantization toggles.
Design ask: Console team to add a 'variant view' toggle so operators can see model variant distribution across regions and tenants during canary.
Security: KMS rotation for quantized artifacts is required; coordinate with Security for approval before canary launch.
